title: agent-kombat roster
description: Shape of a roster preset consumed by scripts/agent-kombat/agent-kombat.sh. A roster names the debaters, the judge and (optionally) the synthesizer, and fixes the round budget. Resolution precedence, first hit wins: --roster-file PATH, then --roster NAME (searched as ./.agent-kombat/rosters/NAME.json for a personal override, then scripts/agent-kombat/rosters/NAME.json for a repo preset), then AGENT_KOMBAT_ROSTER, then the built-in default 'trio-debate'. Per-slot model overrides resolve as --model SLOT_ID=MODEL, then AGENT_KOMBAT_MODEL_<SLOT_ID>, then this file; an unresolved model is a fatal error. This schema is strict (additionalProperties false at both levels) so a typo in a key name is a validation failure rather than a silently ignored setting.

id.description: Stable roster name. Should equal the file basename without .json, because --roster NAME resolves to NAME.json.
id.$comment: The driver does not verify id == basename; keeping them equal is a convention for humans reading logs.

description.description: Why this roster exists and when to pick it over its siblings. Also the place for caveats (e.g. a judge sharing a model with a debater) -- JSON has no comments, so all prose lives here.

rounds.description: Number of debate rounds to run before the judge is asked for a verdict.

max_extra_rounds.description: Upper bound on additional rounds the judge may request when it is not yet ready to rule. 0 disables extension.

debaters.description: Every participant that argues. At least two -- a one-sided 'debate' is out of scope for this tool.

items.$comment: structured_output 'none' is rejected here on purpose: it is only legal on a synthesizer slot, whose output is prose rather than a parsed payload. The driver enforces the same rule.

debaters.$comment: uniqueItems only rejects byte-identical slot objects. The real rule -- slot ids must be unique across debaters + judge + synthesizer -- is a cross-property constraint that JSON Schema cannot express; the driver enforces it and fails with exit code 2.

judge.description: The participant that rules on the debate. Its structured payload carries the 'recommendation' enum that drives the driver's control flow.
judge.$comment: Two rules the driver enforces that are deliberately NOT encoded here. (1) judge.structured_output MUST be 'native': the recommendation enum drives control flow, so a parse miss is an unrecoverable control-flow failure, unlike a debater miss which is recoverable by re-ask. It is left unconstrained in this schema only because --allow-unstructured-judge exists as an explicit escape hatch, and a roster used under that flag must still validate. (2) The driver WARNS (does not fail) when judge.harness and judge.model both equal some debater's pair -- a fresh process buys session independence, not model independence.

synthesizer.description: Optional. Writes the final merged plan. Omit it and the judge slot is reused for synthesis.
synthesizer.$comment: This is the only slot on which structured_output 'none' is legal, because its deliverable is prose (plan-final.md), not a parsed payload.

slot.description: One participant: which CLI to spawn, which model to pin, and how to get structured data back out of it.

id.description: Short slot identifier. Artifact paths derive from it (rounds/r<N>-<id>.turn.json, plan-<id>.md), and it is the key used by --model <id>=<model> and by AGENT_KOMBAT_MODEL_<ID>.

label.description: Anonymous display name shown in prompts, e.g. 'Participant A' or 'Judge'.
label.$comment: MUST NOT be a model or vendor name. Participants and the judge see labels, never slot ids or models -- anonymity is what stops a judge from ruling on brand reputation instead of argument quality.

model.description: Model id passed through to the harness (claude --model, codex exec -m, opencode run -m). Verified locally: claude accepts 'opus' and pinned ids such as 'claude-haiku-4-5-20251001'; codex accepts 'gpt-5.6-sol'; opencode accepts 'deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro' and 'deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash'. opencode model ids have NO cheap-sibling naming convention to exploit: DeepSeek's cheap tier is '-flash', not a '-fast' suffix on the flagship, so nothing may derive a canary model by string-munging this value.

structured_output.description: How the turn payload is obtained. 'native' uses the harness's own schema-constrained output (claude --json-schema, codex exec --output-schema). 'fenced_json' extracts a fenced JSON block out of free-form prose and re-asks on a parse miss -- the only option for opencode, which has no structured-output support at all. 'none' means no payload is parsed.
structured_output.$comment: 'none' is legal ONLY on a synthesizer slot; the driver rejects it on a debater or judge slot. It is present in this enum because $defs/slot is shared by all three positions, and is narrowed to native|fenced_json on the debaters items subschema.

idle_timeout_seconds.description: Kill the turn if the harness produces no output for this long. Raise it for slower or reasoning-heavy models.

reasoning_effort.$comment: ALWAYS set this on a codex slot. ~/.codex/config.toml pins model_reasoning_effort globally (xhigh on this machine), so a codex slot that omits it silently inherits whatever the machine-wide config says and the roster stops being reproducible. Ignored on claude and opencode slots.

variant.description: opencode only -- passed as --variant. Ignored on claude and codex slots. The driver validates the value against the universal reasoning-effort vocabulary (none|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max) because opencode forwards an unknown variant without error and the provider ignores it, so a typo silently runs at the model's default effort. It does NOT validate the per-model subset, and no test pins it: as of 2026-08-21 models.dev reports 'deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro' declaring low|medium|high and 'deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash' high|max, but that is provider metadata which changes with every model release, so encoding it here would reject valid rosters the day a new tier ships. Check the model's current declaration rather than trusting this line.

agent.description: opencode only -- passed as --agent. Required on every opencode slot; the repo ships 'kombat-debater'. Ignored on claude and codex slots.
agent.$comment: Must be exactly 'kombat-debater'. opencode has no read-only sandbox flag, and requiring merely SOME agent is not a guarantee: naming a builtin such as 'build' resolves to {"*": "allow"} (bash and writes enabled) and validation would accept it. The driver enforces this allowlist too (validate_roster).

max_reask.description: How many times to re-ask a slot whose response failed JSON extraction. Only meaningful when structured_output is 'fenced_json'.

allOf.$comment: The 'opencode slots must set agent' rule IS expressible in draft 2020-12, so it is encoded rather than left to prose. The driver enforces it independently (exit code 2) -- keep both in sync, and do not rely on this branch alone, since a bare JSON-syntax check (the repo's pre-commit check-json hook) never evaluates it.

slot.$comment: Harness scoping of reasoning_effort (codex), variant and agent (opencode) is documented per-property but not enforced as a prohibition: a stray key from another harness is inert, and forbidding it here would reject rosters the driver accepts.
